hook.line: Vale is telling a story over coffee, and she tells it in the present tense because it makes it feel like it is happening right in front of you. You can do the same.
hook.es: Ayer voy al mercado y me encuentro a Hernando.
hook.en: So yesterday I go to the market and I bump into Hernando.

examples.es: Le compro un regalo carísimo y ni siquiera me da las gracias.
examples.en: I buy her a really expensive present and she doesn't even say thank you.

examples.es: Ayer voy al mercado y me encuentro a Hernando.
examples.en: So yesterday I go to the market and I bump into Hernando.

examples.es: Entro a la oficina y todos se quedan callados.
examples.en: I walk into the office and everyone goes quiet.

examples.es: Anoche llego a casa y no hay luz.
examples.en: Last night I get home and there's no power.

examples.es: Le escribo a Mariana y ni siquiera me contesta.
examples.en: I write to Mariana and she doesn't even answer me.

examples.es: Entro al café y Simón me grita mi nombre.
examples.en: I walk into the café and Simón shouts my name at me.

rule:
When you tell an anecdote among friends, you can use the present tense for things that already happened. A word like *ayer* or *anoche* still tells the listener when. The present just brings the moment closer, like English "so I walk in and…".
It is casual: stories, complaints, jokes. Once you start, don't flip back and forth inside the same scene.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the historical present: the present tense used with past meaning.

readAndPick.es: Ayer llamo a Vale y no contesta.
options: Tomorrow I'll call Vale and she won't answer.
Yesterday I called Vale and she didn't answer.
I call Vale every day and she doesn't answer.

readAndPick.es: Anoche llego a casa y no hay luz.
options: Tonight I'll get home and there'll be no power.
Last night I got home and there was no power.

readAndPick.es: Mañana llego a casa y te llamo.
options: Yesterday I got home and called you.
Tomorrow I'll get home and call you.

readAndPick.es: Le compro un regalo carísimo y ni siquiera me da las gracias.
options: I'll buy her a really expensive present and she won't even say thank you.
I bought her a really expensive present and she didn't even say thank you.

readAndPick.es: Todos los días llego a las ocho.
options: I got there at eight yesterday.
I get there at eight every day.

readAndPick.es: El otro día voy al banco y está cerrado.
options: The other day I went to the bank and it was closed.
The other day I'll go to the bank and it'll be closed.

readAndPick.es: Ayer entro al café y no hay nadie.
options: I always walk into the café and nobody is there.
Yesterday I walked into the café and nobody was there.

readAndPick.es: Anoche salgo de la oficina y está lloviendo.
options: Last night I left the office and it was raining.
Tonight I'll leave the office and it'll be raining.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell it as a lively story in the present: Ayer ___ al mercado y me encuentro a Hernando. (voy / fui)
yourTurn.answer: Ayer voy al mercado y me encuentro a Hernando.
yourTurn.why: In the story present, both verbs stay in the present.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell it as a story in the present: Last night I get home and there's no power.
yourTurn.answer: Anoche llego a casa y no hay luz.
yourTurn.why: *Anoche* sets the time, and the verbs stay in the present.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell it as a story in the present: I walk into the office and everyone goes quiet.
yourTurn.answer: Entro a la oficina y todos se quedan callados.
yourTurn.why: Both actions are in the present, joined by *y*.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell it as a story in the present: I write to Mariana and she doesn't even answer me.
yourTurn.answer: Le escribo a Mariana y ni siquiera me contesta.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell it as a story in the present, about a woman: I buy her a really expensive present and she doesn't even say thank you.
yourTurn.answer: Le compro un regalo carísimo y ni siquiera me da las gracias.
yourTurn.why: Both verbs are in the present, even though it is a past story.

yourTurn.prompt: Move it into the story present: *Ayer fui al mercado y me encontré a Hernando.*
yourTurn.answer: Ayer voy al mercado y me encuentro a Hernando.
yourTurn.why: Change both verbs to the present and keep *ayer*.

yourTurn.prompt: Move it into the story present: *Anoche llegué a casa y no había luz.*
yourTurn.answer: Anoche llego a casa y no hay luz.
yourTurn.why: Both verbs go to the present, and *había* becomes *hay*.

pitfalls.wrong: Ayer voy por la calle y me encontré a Hernando.
pitfalls.right: Ayer voy por la calle y me encuentro a Hernando.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Pick one tense for the story and stay in it.

pitfalls.wrong: Ayer estoy yendo al mercado y me encuentro a Hernando.
pitfalls.right: Ayer voy al mercado y me encuentro a Hernando.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English likes "I'm going", but Spanish uses the simple present.

pitfalls.wrong: Entro a la oficina y todos quedan callados.
pitfalls.right: Entro a la oficina y todos se quedan callados.
pitfalls.why: Almost. "Go quiet" is *quedarse callado*, so keep the *se*.

personal: Tell a short true story from this week in the present, starting with *Ayer…* or *Anoche…*
